featured.name: Vega
featured.fact: In July 1850, at Harvard, it became the first star other than the Sun to be photographed.

featured.name: Deneb
featured.fact: Its name is Arabic for “tail”: it marks the swan’s tail. Few stars the eye can see are as luminous.

featured.name: Altair
featured.fact: It spins once in under eight hours, so fast that it is over 20% wider at the equator than pole to pole.

featured.name: Albireo
featured.fact: One star to the eye; a small telescope splits it into a gold star and a fainter blue one.

source: Yale Bright Star Catalogue, 5th revised ed. (Hoffleit & Warren 1991), CDS catalogue V/50; facts: see docs/night-sky-facts.md
